newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Eicher Ltd net up 30 percent.
newsitem.headline: India's Eicher Ltd net up 30 percent.

text.p: Indian diversified automotive manufacturer Eicher Ltd on Monday announced a 31 percent increase in net profit to 300.7 million rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) from 229.7 million rupees in the previous year.
Sales grew to 5.58 billion in 1996/97 from 4.64 billion in the previous year, the company said in a statement.
The group also announced a dividend of 30 percent, against a dividend of 20 percent in 1995/96.

The group's sales comprise 4.09 billion rupees from sales of Eicher Tractors Ltd, 990 million rupees from motorcycle maker Royal Enfield Motors, and 490 million rupees from gear manufacturer Ramon and Demm, the company said.
Eicher Ltd was formed through the merger of Eicher Tractors, Royal Enfield and Ramon and Demm. In 1994/95, before the merger, the three companies reported total net profit of 140 million rupees.
Earnings per share on the group's equity capital of 202 million rupees work out to 15 rupees, the company said.
The company's growth in 1996/97 was driven by a 30 percent increase in Eicher Tractors' sales of 35 HP tractors.
This year, the company plans to increase output at Ramon and Demm to 500 tonnes a month from 250 tonnes, and at Royal Enfield as well, the statement said.
